selection_rule: Phase 24 executes only inside the admitted court container. This committed manifest records the one admitted venue -- the container marker, the opt-in environment flag, and the image identity and platform the venue records in the environment -- and `forensics/tools/phase24_guard.py` fails closed unless every one of them is present and matches. Nothing about the downstream-1000 atlas is built, run or probed outside this venue (docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md section 1).
metadata_only_rule: `metadata_only` names the Phase-24 generators that read committed atlases and write a ledger -- they execute nothing, no compiler, no probe, no downstream build -- so the guard admits them on any host exactly as the other strata's obligation generators run host-side in CI's static job. Every execution entry point (the runner `phase24_courts.py`, and every later subphase tool that configures, builds, links or runs a downstream project) is deliberately absent from this list, so a host invocation of one is refused. The seven **pure derivations** that `evidence_determinism.py` regenerates and compares are admitted beside `phase24_obligations.py`, because that gate also runs host-side in CI's static job and they must not refuse there: `downstream_freeze.py`, `downstream_holdout.py`, `downstream_failures.py`, `downstream_reconciliation.py`, `phase24_frf.py`, `downstream_blockers.py` and `render_biggest_movers.py` each read only committed Phase-24 artefacts and write a derived plane -- they fetch nothing, compile nothing, link nothing and run no downstream program, so a host invocation of one executes no command and produces no runtime evidence. `downstream_blockers.py` (24.16) reads the committed Phase-24 planes and writes the shared-blocker analysis `forensics/downstream/shared-blockers.json`; `render_biggest_movers.py` (24.16) reads only that analysis and writes the report `docs/PHASE-24-BIGGEST-MOVERS.md` and the `README.md` block. `downstream_remediation.py` (24.17) reads the committed Phase-24 planes plus the preserved pre-remediation baseline `forensics/downstream/blocker-remediation-baseline.json` and writes the before/after record `forensics/downstream/blocker-remediation.json`: it executes nothing (it does not configure, build, link or run a downstream project), it only reads committed partitions and atlases and subtracts two measured figures, so it is admitted alongside the other pure derivations. `phase24_frf.py` (24.14) drives each Phase-24 plane's own pure checker over the committed artefact and over the controlled mutations its own sensitivity control seeds, and records the FRF chain staging and the Gemel checkpoint projection from the committed registry and the committed `forensics/GEMEL_TRAJECTORY.md`; it opens no store, runs no `gemel` command and executes no probe. `downstream_recipe_campaign.py` (24.18) reads the committed Phase-24 planes plus its preserved pre-campaign baseline `forensics/downstream/recipe-campaign-baseline.json` and its own authored attempt record and writes the admission record `forensics/downstream/recipe-campaign.json`: it executes nothing (it does not fetch, configure, build, link or run a downstream project -- the recipes it admits are built by `downstream_build_link.py`, which imports its catalogue), it only classifies committed evidence and subtracts two measured blocker summaries, so it is admitted alongside the other pure derivations. Any tool that fetches, compiles, links or runs a downstream program (the build/link, runtime, high-value, hostility, candidate-freeze and P1000-run tools) stays deliberately absent and is refused on the host.
non_claims: the admitted venue is a container identity, not a security boundary: it records where Phase 24 runs, not what it may claim
the manifest is authored evidence, not proof the container is unmodified: it binds the venue a receipt names, and the image digest is the stronger binding a later subphase may add
admitting a metadata-only generator on the host is not admitting host execution: that generator runs no command and produces no runtime evidence
